NATIVE.meaning: Designed and manufactured inside the owning engineering tradition.
provenanceRequirements: source naming the builder/manufacturer, or explicit native manufacture statement

LICENSED.meaning: Built locally from an external design or production license.
provenanceRequirements: license/transfer evidence or explicit source statement

IMPORTED.meaning: Externally manufactured hardware installed without implying local design origin.

CAPTURED.meaning: Hardware obtained from an adversarial or nonconsensual source and retained in service or study.

SALVAGED.meaning: Recovered hardware whose original ownership or service history may be incomplete.
provenanceRequirements: original origin retained separately when known

REVERSE_ENGINEERED.meaning: Locally reproduced or adapted from studied external machinery.

HYBRID.meaning: One installation intentionally combines multiple engineering traditions or technology bases.
provenanceRequirements: at least two retained origin records
interface responsibilities and source ancestry remain distinct
do not substitute owner, operator, species or visual style as origin

autoResolveTechnologyBasis: Auto-resolution is allowed only from an explicit authoritative technology-basis field or an exact named-source mapping whose basis status is CONFIRMED.
A race/species name, polity, hull owner, operator, visual style, atmosphere or biology is not sufficient by itself.
If two or more CONFIRMED basis records materially participate in the installation, return MULTI_BASIS rather than selecting a majority basis.
DERIVED mappings may suggest candidate bases but may not populate a live selector as confirmed provenance.
multiOriginPolicy: Keep every origin record and its roles independently addressable.
Do not average provenance status across origins.
Do not replace a captured/imported subsystem's manufacturer with the current vessel owner.
Do not collapse reverse-engineered descendants into the source civilization once local redesign is documented.
Hybrid installations require explicit interface certification across power, timing, control, thermal/service, structural/field and recovery boundaries.
namedRacePolicy: ZWLEI_MURREK remains without an automatic generic technology-basis assignment in this registry; its named hardware profile outranks generic basis styling.
ARNOCK remains without an automatic FTL-family assignment and without a universal all-technology biological-basis assumption.
Future named-race auto-resolution requires a source-backed exact mapping entered explicitly rather than pattern matching on names.

integrationModel.purpose: Physically grounded compatibility checks for mixed-origin transit installations without pretending that provenance alone determines performance.

equations.recoveryCutSet: R_survive = min_k R_k over every required recovery cut-set k

interpretation: Pi_c << 1 indicates interface propagation delay is small relative to control response time; Pi_c near or above 1 demands regional autonomy or slower authority loops.
Pi_t << 1 indicates timing jitter is small relative to the phase/coherence window; rising Pi_t consumes calculation and control margin.
M_T <= 0 means at least one coupled subsystem is outside its certified thermal/service envelope.
M_P <= 0 means nominal operation consumes power needed for protected recovery or exceeds available supply.
R_survive is a weakest-cut-set quantity; abundant reserve in one origin cannot replace a missing recovery path in another.

prohibitedShortcuts: captured hardware becomes native by continued use
majority component count determines safety authority

canonGuards: Preserve named-source canon over generic technology-basis inference.
Never assign an FTL family from technology ancestry alone.
Never assign a technology basis from race/species identity alone unless a higher-authority source explicitly establishes that mapping.
Mixed-origin and hybrid installations must retain every material ancestry record in exports.
Proposed compatibility mathematics are engineering models, not setting-wide measured constants.
Missing interface data must produce UNRESOLVED rather than zero or assumed compatibility.
A compatible interface does not imply common origin; an incompatible interface does not disprove historical integration if an adapter is documented.
Human-readable translation may not replace native control state or provenance.
Manufacturer, operator, owner, inventor and maintainer are separate roles unless a source explicitly unifies them.
